metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.candidate_universe: Preserved candidate universe and findings from certified legacy work unit ecosystem-external--part-3--java; recertification did not select a new language-specific target.

component_findings.current_knowledge: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-3--java): Java exhibits an exceptionally deep and broad publicly available knowledge base across all three predeclared indicator families: it is among the top handful of languages by cumulative Stack Overflow Q&A volume, it sustains one of the largest single-language-dedicated public subreddits with 18 years of continuous activity, its vendor (Oracle) maintains a complete and actively updated public documentation stack (JLS, Java Tutorials, dev.java, Javadoc tooling), and it is unusual among languages in supporting a mature worldwide network of volunteer user groups plus multiple long-running (decades-old) global conferences and a formal community-recognition program (Java Champions). The score is set

metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.limitations: Raw SO tag counts are a partial proxy: newer/faster-growing tags (e.g., Python, TypeScript) are gaining share and per-quarter pageview leaderboards have shifted away from Java toward Python/JS/Git-related questions since ~2018-2020, so absolute volume overstates current-day relative mindshare growth even though it still reflects an enormous historical and ongoing archive. | Subreddit membership counts are a raw popularity indicator and are not used alone; they are combined with the other two indicator families. | Stack Overflow tag counts and subreddit subscriber counts are raw popularity/volume indicators; per methodology they are not used standalone but combined with qualitative documentation-completeness and community-infrastructure evidence collected via the same retrieval route and depth that would be applied to every other language in this metric.
metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.selection_rule: Inspect the same knowledge channels for every language and use current, publicly accessible evidence rather than raw search-result counts alone.

snapshot_recertification.policy: legacy evidence re-adjudicated under current runner-owned rubric
